text: Shopkeeper is a billing assistant for one-person businesses. You type one sentence. Shopkeeper does the PayPal work.
A tutor or a freelance designer gets paid for many small jobs. Each job needs an invoice, a due date, and often a reminder. Many owners skip the reminder. Then the money comes late.
This is the live demo on the PayPal sandbox. I ask for an invoice for two hours of tutoring at 45 dollars per hour, due Friday.
The agent calls the PayPal Invoicing API. It creates the invoice and sends it. The invoice number and the total come from PayPal, not from the model.
Next, I ask which invoices are still unpaid. Shopkeeper shows a table with the total, the due date, and the status.
I ask for a friendly reminder. Shopkeeper finds the invoice and sends a PayPal reminder.
Shopkeeper also makes checkout links. One sentence gives a PayPal checkout link for a sticker pack.
say: Shopkeeper also makes checkout links. One sentence gives a PayPal checkout link for a nine fifty sticker pack.

text: Some actions close a bill or move money back. When I ask to cancel an invoice, the agent stops and shows an approval card.
After I click Approve, the agent cancels the invoice in PayPal. Refunds use the same approval step.
Each browser gets its own agent on a Cloudflare Durable Object. Gemini picks the PayPal tools through the Vercel AI SDK. If one model is busy, the agent tries the next model.
Shopkeeper is open source under the MIT license. Try the live demo, and read the code on GitHub.
